title: Aniridia: The PAX6 Pan-Ocular Syndrome
summary: Aniridia is a complex, bilateral pan-ocular disorder caused by a haploinsufficiency of the PAX6 gene (11p13). Beyond the striking absence of the iris, it involves progressive keratopathy, glaucoma, cataracts, and foveal hypoplasia, requiring lifelong multidisciplinary management.

sections.title: Clinical Definition & Overview
sections.content: Aniridia is a congenital, bilateral condition characterized by the partial or complete absence of the iris. However, the term 'aniridia' is a misnomer as it is a global pan-ocular developmental defect affecting the cornea, anterior chamber angle, lens, retina, and optic nerve. It is most commonly inherited in an autosomal dominant fashion (85%) with high penetrance but variable expressivity.

rows: 30% of sporadic cases involve WT1 gene deletions

sections.title: Mandatory Diagnostic Workup
content: Step 1: Clinical Exam (Slit lamp for iris stump, Gonioscopy for angle)
Step 2: Pediatric Genetic Testing (PAX6 sequencing & FISH for 11p13 deletion)
Step 3: Imaging (OCT of macula for foveal hypoplasia; UBM for iris stump)
Step 4: Systemic Screening (Renal Ultrasound for Wilms Tumor)
Step 5: Functional Assessment (Visual acuity, Nystagmus evaluation)

sections.title: Critical: WAGR Screening Protocol
content: MANDATORY: Renal Ultrasound every 3 months until age 8 in sporadic cases.
Risk of Wilms Tumor is 50% in WAGR (deletion of 11p13 including WT1).
Monitor for Nephropathy and Gonadoblastoma.
Developmental delays require early intervention services.

sections.title: Management Strategy
content: Optical: Tinted lenses/CL for photophobia.
Corneal: Preservative-free lubricants; Autologous serum.
LSCD: Limbal Stem Cell Transplant (KLAL or Cincinatti technique).
Glaucoma: Prostaglandins/Beta-blockers; Gonio-surgery early; GDD/Tube shunts for refractory cases.
Cataract: Careful MICS; specialized iris-prosthetic IOLs (e.g., Morcher/Ophtec).

content.explanation: W: Wilms Tumor, A: Aniridia, G: Genitourinary anomalies (cryptorchidism), R: Range of developmental delays (formerly Mental Retardation).

sections.title: Surgical Pearls: Cataract & Iris Prosthesis
content: Zonular instability is common; use Capsule Tension Rings (CTR).
Artificial Iris Implants (HumanOptics) can be sutured or placed in-the-bag.
Avoid iris implants if glaucoma is uncontrolled.
High risk of Aniridic Fibrosis Syndrome (AFS) post-surgery.

sections.title: Prognosis & Red Flags
content: Sudden vision loss: Rule out retinal detachment or acute glaucoma.
Progressive corneal whitening: Indicative of AAK progression.
Avoid routine use of Pilocarpine (may worsen angle crowding).
Guarded prognosis for penetrating keratoplasty (PK) due to LSC deficiency.

sections.title: Landmark Insights & Recent Advances
content: Nonsense Suppression Therapy: Ataluren (PTC124) shows promise in restoring PAX6 function in PTC mutations.
Boston Keratoprosthesis (Type 1): Often preferred over standard PK for end-stage AAK.
Gene Therapy: Research into CRISPR/Cas9 to correct PAX6 haploinsufficiency is ongoing.
Epidemiology Note: Gillespie Syndrome is NOT associated with Wilms Tumor risk.
